title: Refuse to publish when lore-cli's version differs from quest's (Article 3.6)
description: Constitution Article 3 clause 6 (opum-ai/opum-agent 73ba142): each CLI release workflow refuses to publish when the two version numbers differ; the check, not the prose, keeps the pair together. lore-cli builds the mirror check; the mechanism is agreed with lore-cli directly (proposal sent 2026-09-27: compare own package.json version to the peer package.json on the peer main via the GitHub contents API, fail closed on any read error, dry runs included, no override flag).

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/publish-release.mjs refuses, dry run included, when lore-cli's version on the agreed ref differs from quest's package.json version, naming both versions and the refs read
release.yml runs the same check before any npm publish
Any failure to read the peer version refuses rather than passes, and tests cover match, mismatch and read failure
The mechanism matches what lore-cli built, confirmed with lore-cli

implementationNotes: Built to the mechanism proposed to lore-cli on 2026-09-27. No reply yet: lore-cli is blocked on its own user's version prompt, per opum-agent. scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs reads @opum-ai/lore package.json on opum-ai/lore-cli main through the gh contents API, raw. It refuses on a mismatch, a read failure, malformed JSON, another package name or a missing version. publish-release.mjs runs it first, before the receipt, credential or any publish, in dry runs too. release.yml runs it with --require before its first npm publish. Evidence: test/qcli386-version-parity.test.ts, 8 tests. Mutation control: disabling the mismatch comparison turned exactly the mismatch test red. A live run refused as expected: quest 0.10.0, lore 0.9.3 on lore-cli main. bun run check exit 0, 753 tests. AC4 stays OPEN until lore-cli confirms its mirror reads quest-cli main the same way.

Both directions measured live on 2026-09-27. Refused while lore main was 0.9.3 (quest 0.10.0 read, earlier today). After lore main moved to 0.11.0 at c9b9377: "quest 0.11.0 and lore 0.11.0 (opum-ai/lore-cli@main:package.json) are one version (Article 3.6)", exit 0. lore-cli agreed the mechanism and is mirroring it as LCLI-613. AC4 closes on their landing SHAs.

HANDOFF at the session recycle, 2026-09-27. Left In Progress on purpose. ACs 1-3 are checked with evidence. The gate was measured live both ways: it refused at lore 0.9.3, and passed "quest 0.11.0 and lore 0.11.0 ... are one version" once lore main moved to c9b9377. It gated the real 0.11.0 staging. AC4 waits on lore-cli. They agreed the mechanism on 2026-09-27 and are mirroring it as LCLI-613 (a read of opum-ai/quest-cli main package.json via the contents API, raw, with .name == "@opum-ai/quest", failing closed, dry runs included, no override), and promised to send their landing SHAs. NEXT: when the SHAs arrive, read lore-cli scripts/publish-release.sh and release.yml at those SHAs by API, confirm they match, then check AC4 and complete.

OPAG-465 AC1 (constitution Article 3.6), demonstrated 2026-09-27 with nothing published: the release path REFUSES a mismatched pair. The gate is scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs requireVersionParity, which scripts/publish-release.mjs:536 calls first, in dry runs too. It compares this checkout's package.json against opum-ai/lore-cli@main:package.json, and that read 0.11.0. Run in a disposable copy (git archive origin/dev 3bd59d7 into scratch, git init), never in this tree. MISMATCH, with scratch package.json set to 0.11.1: `node scripts/qualification/version-parity.mjs --require` exits 1 with "Refusing to publish: quest is 0.11.1 (this checkout's package.json) but lore is 0.11.0 (opum-ai/lore-cli@main:package.json); Article 3.6: lore and quest publish at one version, or not at all". `node scripts/publish-release.mjs` (dry run) exits 1 with "Refusing to publish 0.11.1: " and the same text. MATCHED, with 0.11.0 restored: the standalone check exits 0 with "quest 0.11.0 and lore 0.11.0 (opum-ai/lore-cli@main:package.json) are one version (Article 3.6)." The publisher dry run prints the same pass line, then stops at the NEXT gate, "--receipt <path> is required", with exit 2. So parity passed and did not decide that run. FAIL-CLOSED: requireVersionParity against the nonexistent ref no-such-ref-qcli394 returns ok:false, "lore's version could not be read ... (HTTP 404); Article 3.6 refuses rather than assumes". promote-release.mjs (the latest move) was not exercised. This demonstrates the publish step only.

Paused 2026-09-27. lore-cli confirmed AC4 directly, reading lore-cli 70c82443 and quest-cli e0e3a44 (whose scripts are unchanged at main 41887c9). The rule, the peer ref (main, via the contents API), fail-closed behaviour with no override, and placement first in publish-release (dry run included) all match. Checked here against the source rather than relayed: lore's test/fixtures/quest-cli/version-parity.mjs is byte-identical to ours at main; our blob is still 249c28dc, the one lore's header cites; checkVersionParity is the same rule with the roles swapped. ONE REAL DIVERGENCE, on lore's side and confirmed in the file: lore's release.yml runs parity inside the publish job gated by `if: inputs.publish == true` (lore-cli release.yml:745), so a publish:false dispatch skips it. Ours (release.yml:160) runs on every dispatch. Neither side can PUBLISH a mismatched pair, and lore's publish-release.sh --dry-run does run parity, but a lore dry dispatch goes green on mismatched versions. AC4 is left unticked and routed to opum-agent, which rules whether that blocks "the mechanism matches". Other differences, all named in lore's header: --version input from publish-release.sh, a checklist/verify-only exemption (both write nothing), and a pinned --hostname (ours is QCLI-396, now extended to readPeerVersion).
